# PSDG — Philosopher's Stone Dice Game

> A small deterministic dice game with an exact solver, used as a benchmark for two measurable
> failure modes. (1) Representation insufficiency: a tabular learner that solves the game from
> the full state fails when it observes only the dice tops, because the rules make an early,
> hidden commitment (a die's "facing") decide the outcome later — an information loss that shows
> up as an enumerable regret floor, not a training artifact. (2) Deployment fragility: an exact,
> oracle-derived plan becomes exploitable when it is frozen instead of re-solved after the
> opponent leaves the expected line. Because the game is solved, both failures are measured
> against exact ground truth and (for the representation case) bounded below by enumeration.

## Repository and code

- [solvers/python/solver.py — the exact solver](https://github.com/Rob-McCormack/psdg/blob/main/solvers/python/solver.py)

## Key results
- Representation: the full-state learner reaches 0 regret / 100% win on every seed and every
  training budget; the tops-only learner never does — 0 of 5 seeds reach optimal even at 8x the
  converged budget. The training-proof anchor is an enumerated lower bound: Exchange floor 0.021,
  Draft floor 0.0097 (oracle win/loss units) on the demo opening, which no memoryless tops-only
  policy can beat. The trained loss rate (2-6%) is budget-sensitive and is not the headline.
- Deployment: on one 5000-game suite, a frozen static plan concedes 8.5% / 6.9% B-wins versus
  5.7% when A re-solves; the draw-independent existence result is 320 of 3663 A-win openings
  beatable by at least one worse B move under static deployment.
